title: throughput-bisect-cbatch-notes
content:
Purpose: scratchpad while bisecting a throughput regression that appears after the 2026-02-10 deployment. Focus: continuous batching (cbatch) misconfig and autoscaler interactions.

Summary (current hypothesis):
- Symptoms: host-level throughput (tokens/sec) dropped ~40% for short-seq chat workloads starting ~2026-02-10. Latency SLOs mostly met but cost/per-token increased.
- Root suspicion: continuous batching was effectively disabled/fragmented (microbatches) due to a combination of: a recent autoscaler pod label change + cbatch feature-flag evaluation order + KV cache TTL reset.
- Plan: bisect config + roll forward small fixes, verify with synthetic load.

Observed numbers (perf baseline vs current):
- Baseline (2026-02-01): avg tokens/sec per GPU (g4dn-like) for 1k qps short-chats: 1150–1300 tps, median 1200 tps.
- After regression (2026-02-12): avg 700–780 tps, median 730 tps.
- CPU usage on host up ~12%, GPU SM util down ~20% (weird).
- Average batch size sent to runtime: dropped from ~18 tokens/batch -> ~3 tokens/batch (probable cause).

Commands run so far (notes + outputs):
- Quick check: tail logs for runtime pod (serving-runtime-v2-rc1)
  $ kubectl -n prod logs serving-runtime-v2-rc1 -c runtime --since=2h | grep -E "batch|cbatch|kvcache" -n | tail -n 50
  [sample output]
  2026-03-03T14:12:01Z INFO batcher: flush triggered due to time_budget_ms=10, batch_size=2
  2026-03-03T14:12:01Z DEBUG cbatch: queue_len=1, current_wait_ms=9
  2026-03-03T14:12:01Z INFO kvcache: miss for key session:abc123

- Noticed many "flush triggered due to time_budget_ms" events with very small batch_size. Time budget looks low (10 ms). We expect dynamic time_budget scaling to 30–50 ms under low latency target.

- Check deployment config / feature flags on configmap:
  $ kubectl -n prod get configmap serving-runtime-config -o yaml | sed -n '1,120p'
  key: continuous_batching.enabled: "true"
  key: continuous_batching.time_budget_ms: "10"  # suspicious
  key: continuous_batching.min_batch_size: "8"
  key: cbatch.eval_order: "client_first"
  key: autoscaler.pod-labels: "tier=fast,cbatch-disabled=false"

- Hypothesis: time_budget_ms was accidentally set to 10 in a config promotion on 2026-02-10. Also "client_first" eval order may read client headers that are missing and short-circuit cbatch.

Bisect steps taken: (notes of experiments)
1) Locally override time_budget_ms -> 50ms on a single canary pod and run synthetic load (wrk-like):
  $ curl -X POST https://canary.example/api/override -d '{"continuous_batching.time_budget_ms": 50}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'
  Result: batch_size median increased to 12, tokens/sec rose from 720 -> 1080. Latency p95 rose ~3ms but still within SLO. Conclusion: time_budget is a major lever.

2) Switch eval_order -> "server_first" to force cbatch to consider server side queueing instead of client hints (small A/B):
  $ kubectl -n prod set env deployment/serving-runtime EVAL_ORDER=server_first
  Result: small improvement (batch median 14), tokens/sec ~1120. Combined with time_budget=50ms we see ~1220 (close to baseline).

3) Reproduce the issue without KV cache: force kvcache miss storm by clearing cache on one pod:
  $ kubectl exec -it serving-runtime-v2-rc1 -- /bin/sh -c 'curl localhost:9000/kvcache/clear'
  Observation: throughput dropped further to ~600 tps, cpu increased, doc shows a pattern where many requests rebuild KV cache and then small batches appear. Suggests KV cache TTL reset on 2026-02-10.

4) Inspect git history for config changes around 2026-02-10:
  $ git --no-pager log -n 30 --pretty="%h %ad %s" --date=short -- config/continuous_batching.yaml
  9f7a2d1 2026-02-10 "tweak cbatch defaults for latency regression"  <-- suspicious
  4ab3c6f 2026-01-28 "initial cbatch A/B config"
  Patch 9f7a2d1 shows default time_budget_ms=10 and eval_order=client_first (commit notes: "lower time budget to favor latency").

Important log snippets (from runtime with timestamps):
- 2026-03-03T14:12:01Z INFO batcher: scheduled flush (queue_len=1) wait_ms=9 reason=budget_expire
- 2026-03-03T14:12:01Z WARN cbatch: client_hint_missing for request id=... fallback_to_immediate
- 2026-03-03T14:12:02Z INFO autoscaler: scale_event pod_label_change detected: tier=fast->tier=burst (2026-02-11 02:18:00)

Inference from logs: autoscaler relabelling on 2026-02-11 plus the tightened time_budget caused continuous batching to rarely accumulate messages before forced flush. Additionally, client-first evaluation path falls back if client hints missing which causes even more flushes.

Further experiments to run (next actions):
- Controlled rollout: set continuous_batching.time_budget_ms=55 and eval_order=server_first on one full node group (not single pod) with metric collection. Compare tokens/sec + median batch size + p95 lat.
- Add an override that forces min_batch_size=6 for 10 minutes to see smoothing effect.
- Re-run with kvcache warming steps: pre-warm top-50 keys to reduce miss storm and observe batch size.
- Re-run with autoscaler label lock: prevent label shift for a minute to see if pod relabelling interacts with request routing (we've seen routing changes that hit different nodepool with different load balancers/connection behavior).

Hypotheses to confirm/deny:
- H1 (confirmed-ish): time_budget_ms=10 introduced on 2026-02-10 is primary cause. Changing it increases avg batch sizes and throughput.
- H2 (probable): eval_order=client_first causes fallback flushes when client hints are not present, exacerbating small batches. Switching to server_first helps.
- H3 (possible): autoscaler pod-label changes rerouted traffic to a nodepool where some connection-level settings (keepalive, HTTP/2 window) differ, causing request patterns that reduce natural batching. Need to validate with LB logs.
- H4 (likely): KV cache reset/miss storm increasing per-request work and interfering with quick batch formation. Warming reduces impact.

Quick artifacts to collect for postmortem: (what I already grabbed + missing)
- git commit 9f7a2d1 full diff (already saved locally).
- ConfigMap history 2026-01 -> 2026-03 (kubectl rollout history?)
- Load test scripts & raw output (wrk, perf numbers) for baseline, time_budget override, eval_order override.
- LB access logs around 2026-02-11 to see routing label change correlation.
- Pod level metrics: per-request latency distribution, batch_size histogram, KV cache hit/miss ratio per minute (prometheus queries).

Prometheus queries to run (examples):
- avg(rate(tokens_generated_total[1m])) by (pod)
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pod))
- sum(rate(cbatch_batch_size_sum[5m]))/sum(rate(cbatch_batch_size_count[5m]))  -> avg batch size
- sum(rate(kvcache_miss_total[5m])) by (pod)

Notes about potential rollout fix:
- Immediate mitigation: bump continuous_batching.time_budget_ms to 50 and set eval_order=server_first clusterwide. Monitor for 30 minutes; rollback if latency regresses. Communicate to SRE/incident channel "cbatch-timebudget-50-rollout".
- Medium-term: change config promotion process to gate cbatch default changes behind load tests (automated) and require an entry in the config change log with perf benchmarks.
- Long-term: make cbatch dynamic auto-tuner that adjusts time_budget based on observed queue_len and p95 latency targets.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why was time_budget changed? Who approved 9f7a2d1? (owner tag in git points to @ejohnson) Need to ask if this was expected.
- Did autoscaler label change intentionally trigger tier switch for this nodepool? SRE ticket referenced but not linked in commit.
- Are there any client SDK changes that removed client hints which would make client_first less effective? Check SDK release notes around Feb 9–11.

Scratch TODOs (practical):
- [ ] Run cluster-wide time_budget=50 experiment (30m) and capture metrics (owner: Lucas)
- [ ] Request LB logs from infra for 2026-02-10..2026-02-12 window (owner: Sana)
- [ ] Open PR to set eval_order default to server_first and add test (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Draft postmortem note with timeline and mitigation (owner: Lucas)

Random breadcrumbs that may matter later:
- I saw a code path where cbatch checks Connection: keep-alive vs http2 pseudo header and treats http2 as no-client-hint. If the LB switched to HTTP/2 abruptly, that could explain more fallback flushes. Save this in case.
- There is a small race in batcher when queue_len metric is sampled concurrently with flush; it can underreport and trigger earlier flushes. Not high prob, but mention in postmortem.

End of scratchpad. Will update as I run the cluster experiment.
